beats.title: The Hadean Begins
beats.description: A newborn planet is a molten, battered ball under constant bombardment, with no stable crust and no oceans yet.
beats.note: Start given as about 4.6 billion years ago; Earth formed c. 4.567 Ga. Years are negative years before present.

beats.title: The Archean Begins
beats.description: The first lasting crust forms under young oceans, and single-celled microbes are the only life on a planet with no free oxygen.
beats.note: 4031 Ma on the ICS chart; shared with the Eoarchean, so one beat.

beats.title: The Paleoarchean Begins
beats.description: Stable continental fragments grow, and microbial mats build the first layered stromatolite reefs in shallow seas.

beats.title: The Mesoarchean Begins
beats.description: Photosynthesising microbes spread through the oceans while the first large, enduring landmasses take shape.

beats.title: The Neoarchean Begins
beats.description: Continents grow quickly as crust is built and recycled, and oxygen-making microbes multiply in the seas.

beats.title: The Proterozoic Begins
beats.description: Oxygen from tiny sea-dwellers starts to build up in the air, and the old chemistry of the planet is slowly rewritten.
beats.note: Shared with the Paleoproterozoic and Siderian; one beat.

beats.title: The Rhyacian Begins
beats.description: Oxygen is now in the air for good, and ice sheets reach the tropics in one of the planet's earliest great glaciations.

beats.title: The Orosirian Begins
beats.description: Mountain belts rise as continents collide, and a huge asteroid leaves a vast crater in what is now South Africa.

beats.title: The Statherian Begins
beats.description: Continents gather into a large landmass, and the seas hold more complex cells than ever before.

beats.title: The Mesoproterozoic Begins
beats.description: A long, calm stretch of stable climate and ocean chemistry opens, with cells growing more complex beneath the waves.
beats.why_in: start of the Mesoproterozoic era and Calymmian period
beats.note: Named for the era; shares its start with the Calymmian.

beats.title: The Ectasian Begins
beats.description: Shallow seas spread over stable continental shelves, and early algae thrive in them.

beats.title: The Stenian Begins
beats.description: Continents crash together to build the supercontinent Rodinia, and the first sexually reproducing algae appear.

beats.title: The Neoproterozoic Begins
beats.description: The supercontinent Rodinia sits largely intact and begins to split apart, setting up the world's coldest spells.
beats.why_in: start of the Neoproterozoic era and Tonian period
beats.note: Shares its start with the Tonian.

beats.title: The Cryogenian, Snowball Earth
beats.description: Ice sheets creep to the equator and may freeze almost the whole planet, in the deepest cold the world has known.

beats.title: The Ediacaran Begins
beats.description: As the great ice melts, soft-bodied frond and disc creatures appear on the sea floor, the first large complex life.

beats.title: The Cambrian Begins
beats.description: Animals with shells, eyes and legs suddenly fill warm shallow seas in a burst of new body plans.
beats.why_in: start of the Cambrian, Paleozoic and Phanerozoic
beats.note: 538.8 Ma; shared with Phanerozoic and Paleozoic, one beat.

beats.title: The Furongian Begins
beats.description: Trilobites dominate warm shallow seas, and reef-like mounds of microbes and sponges spread across drowned continental shelves.

beats.title: The Ordovician Begins
beats.description: Seas teem with trilobites, corals and early fishes, and warm shallow oceans cover much of the land.

beats.title: The Silurian Begins
beats.description: Life recovers from a glacial mass dying, jawed fishes diversify, and the first plants creep onto damp ground.

beats.title: The Devonian Begins
beats.description: Fishes flourish in the seas, and the first forests and fish with limbs set the stage for life to walk on land.

beats.title: The Late Devonian Begins
beats.description: Tree-sized forests spread across the continents while armoured fishes rule seas that are about to suffer repeated crises.
beats.why_in: start of the Late Devonian epoch

beats.title: The Carboniferous Begins
beats.description: Vast swampy forests spread across the land, giant dragonflies fly overhead, and the dead plants will become coal.

beats.title: The Pennsylvanian Begins
beats.description: Coal swamps blanket low-lying lands, and the first reptiles lay shelled eggs that can hatch away from water.
beats.why_in: start of the Pennsylvanian (Late Carboniferous) epoch

beats.title: The Permian Begins
beats.description: Landmasses merge into one supercontinent, and dry interiors favour reptiles and the sail-backed relatives of mammals.

beats.title: The Lopingian Begins
beats.description: A single giant landmass bakes under a hot, dry climate while volcanoes in the far east start to belch lava.
beats.why_in: start of the Lopingian (Late Permian) epoch

beats.title: The Triassic Begins
beats.description: A barren, hot world slowly refills after the worst extinction in history, and the first dinosaurs and mammals appear.
beats.why_in: start of the Triassic, shared with the Mesozoic
beats.note: 251.9 Ma; shared with the Mesozoic, one beat.

beats.title: The Late Triassic Begins
beats.description: Monsoon rains fall on the great supercontinent, and early dinosaurs share it with crocodile-like rivals.
beats.why_in: start of the Late Triassic epoch

beats.title: The Jurassic Begins
beats.description: The supercontinent starts to break up, ferns and conifers cover the land, and giant long-necked dinosaurs roam.

beats.title: The Middle Jurassic Begins
beats.description: Rising seas flood the continental edges while long-necked giants and early feathered relatives of birds spread.
beats.why_in: start of the Middle Jurassic epoch

beats.title: The Late Jurassic Begins
beats.description: The Atlantic widens, warm seas deepen, and plated and long-necked giants graze lush floodplains.
beats.why_in: start of the Late Jurassic epoch

beats.title: The Cretaceous Begins
beats.description: Flowering plants and bees spread, warm seas flood the continents, and chalk piles up on the sea floor.

beats.title: The Late Cretaceous Begins
beats.description: Sea levels peak and the climate is a greenhouse, as the great horned and tyrant dinosaurs rise to rule.
beats.why_in: start of the Late Cretaceous epoch

beats.title: The Paleogene Begins
beats.description: After a giant impact wipes out the big dinosaurs, small mammals and birds inherit a changed world.
beats.why_in: start of the Paleogene, Cenozoic and Paleocene
beats.note: 66 Ma; shared with the Cenozoic and Paleocene, one beat.

beats.title: The Eocene Begins
beats.description: A burst of global heating gives the planet lush forests to the poles, and early horses, whales and primates spread.

beats.title: The Oligocene Begins
beats.description: Ice sheets grow on Antarctica as the climate cools, and open grassy woodland starts to replace tropical forest.

beats.title: The Neogene Begins
beats.description: Grasslands sweep across the continents, and apes diversify as mountain belts such as the Alps keep rising.
beats.why_in: start of the Neogene period and Miocene epoch
beats.note: 23.04 Ma; shared with the Miocene, one beat.

beats.title: The Pliocene Begins
beats.description: The Mediterranean refills, the climate cools, and upright-walking ape ancestors of humans appear in Africa.

beats.title: The Pleistocene, the Ice Age
beats.description: Ice sheets advance and retreat over the northern lands, woolly mammoths roam, and the human genus appears.
beats.why_in: start of the Pleistocene epoch and Quaternary
beats.note: 2.58 Ma; shared with the Quaternary, one beat.

beats.title: The Holocene Begins
beats.description: The great ice sheets retreat for good, and a mild, steady climate lets farming and cities take root.
beats.note: 11,700 years before 2000, i.e. about 9700 BCE; the other beats are in years before present.
